claims.claim: A Python comparison produces a Boolean value.
Python uses truth-value testing when an expression is used in a Boolean context.
A conditional decision selects one outcome when its condition is true and another when it is false.
Python's conditional expression has the form x if condition else y and evaluates the condition before selecting one of the two expressions.
The expression not x produces a Boolean truth-test result, while and and or can return one of their operands.
The official tutorial presents if/elif/else mechanics; detailed branch syntax is deliberately reserved for the adjacent lesson.
